articles.title: Choosing Azure app hosting: App Service vs Container Apps vs AKS vs Container Instances vs Functions
articles.scope: Decision guide across control, scaling model, networking, cost floor and operational burden for App Service, Container Apps, AKS Automatic and Standard, Container Instances and Functions (including Functions on Container Apps), with a batch branch covering Container Apps jobs, ACI, Kubernetes Jobs and Azure Batch (owned by cloud/azure/compute). Each option carries its AWS counterpart and fidelity; reader can justify a hosting or batch choice for AZ-305.

articles.title: Azure App Service: plans, tiers, scaling and the hosting model
articles.scope: App Service plans and tiers (Free/Shared, Basic, Standard, Premium v3/v4, Isolated v2 on App Service Environment v3), Windows vs Linux, code vs containers with sidecars, and how apps share a plan. Contrasts scale up vs scale out, rule-based Azure Monitor autoscale vs automatic scaling, zone redundancy and per-app scaling; maps to Elastic Beanstalk (partial).

articles.title: Configure App Service: custom domains, TLS, networking, built-in authentication, backup and deployment slots
articles.scope: Map custom DNS names, bind managed or Key Vault certificates, enforce TLS, and choose VNet integration (outbound) vs private endpoints (inbound) vs access restrictions. Configure built-in authentication with Entra ID, app settings and Key Vault references, backup and restore, and deployment slots with sticky settings, swap with preview, auto swap and traffic routing, in Bicep and CLI.

articles.title: Azure Container Instances: container groups, restart policies, sizing, Spot and confidential SKUs, NGroups, standby pools and virtual nodes
articles.scope: Provision single and multi-container groups with CPU/memory sizing, restart policies, secure environment values, Azure Files volumes, managed-identity ACR pull, zonal placement and VNet deployment (NAT gateway is the only supported egress). Covers regular, confidential and Spot SKUs, NGroups fleets with rolling upgrades, standby pools, virtual nodes for AKS burst, the retired GPU SKUs and SC-500 security controls; maps to standalone Fargate tasks (partial).

articles.title: Azure Container Registry: SKUs, ACR Tasks, geo-replication and image trust
articles.scope: Build, push, version and manage images and OCI artifacts across Basic, Standard and Premium with geo-replication, private endpoints, repository-scoped tokens vs Entra RBAC/ABAC, artifact cache and purge; run ACR Tasks (quick, triggered, multi-step) from C# and Python pipelines. Moves signing to Notary Project because Docker Content Trust cannot be enabled on new or never-enabled registries from May 31, 2026 and is removed March 31, 2028; adds Defender for Containers scanning and the Amazon ECR contrast.

articles.title: Azure Container Apps: environments, revisions, KEDA scaling, Dapr, jobs and dynamic sessions
articles.scope: Workload profiles environments (default; Consumption and Dedicated profiles, serverless GPUs) vs legacy Consumption-only environments, ingress, secrets and managed identity, revision modes with traffic splitting and labels, KEDA scale rules including scale to zero, Dapr sidecars, jobs and dynamic sessions as sandboxes for agent code. Reader can deploy an API, an event-driven worker and an agent tool sandbox and explain the AKS and ECS differences.

articles.title: Azure Kubernetes Service: architecture, AKS Automatic vs Standard, and the operating model
articles.scope: Control plane tiers, system vs user node pools, AKS Automatic vs Standard, Azure CNI Overlay and Cilium (kubenet retires March 31, 2028), Entra Workload ID, node auto-provisioning vs cluster autoscaler, upgrade channels and LTS, add-ons (KEDA, Istio; Open Service Mesh ends September 30, 2027), Container insights, managed Prometheus and Fleet Manager. Ingress is delegated to the AKS ingress article; contrasts with EKS and EKS Auto Mode.

articles.title: AKS ingress after ingress-nginx: application routing (NGINX and Gateway API), Application Gateway for Containers and Istio Gateway API
articles.scope: Explains the upstream Ingress NGINX retirement (maintenance ended March 2026) and Microsoft's critical-patch support for app routing NGINX through November 2026, then compares the migration targets: the app routing Gateway API implementation, Application Gateway for Containers and Istio Gateway API ingress. Covers DNS and Key Vault TLS integration, feature gaps and a migration runbook.

articles.title: Securing AKS: Entra ID and Azure RBAC for Kubernetes, private clusters, network policy, Azure Policy, image integrity, node upgrades and Defender for Containers
articles.scope: Configure Entra integration with Kubernetes RBAC or Azure RBAC, disable local accounts, and restrict the API server with private clusters, API server VNet integration or authorized IP ranges. Apply Cilium or Calico network policies, the Azure Policy add-on and pod security admission, Workload ID with the Key Vault Secrets Store CSI provider, Notation/Ratify verification, node OS auto-upgrade and the Defender sensor; bridges SC-500 to CKS.

articles.title: Deploy and troubleshoot containers on App Service, Container Apps and AKS
articles.scope: Deploy one image three ways: to App Service with managed-identity ACR pull, app settings as environment variables, Key Vault references and sidecars; to Container Apps with CLI and Bicep; and to AKS with manifests and Helm using Workload ID. Troubleshoot with kubectl logs/events/describe, Container Apps log streams and console, App Service diagnostics, connectivity checks and Container insights KQL.

articles.title: Azure Functions hosting: Flex Consumption vs Premium vs Dedicated vs Container Apps vs Consumption (legacy)
articles.scope: Scaling, cold start, memory, timeouts, VNet, containers, slots and billing per plan: Flex is Linux-only with per-function scaling to 1,000 instances, 512/2,048/4,096 MB sizes, always ready instances and rolling updates instead of slots. Covers legacy Consumption (only serverless Windows option; Linux Consumption retires September 30, 2028; v3 Linux apps stopped after September 30, 2026) and in-process end of support on November 10, 2026.

articles.title: Azure Functions: triggers, bindings, identity-based connections and deployment
articles.scope: Build serverless APIs and event handlers with HTTP, timer, Service Bus, Event Grid, Event Grid-based Blob and Cosmos DB triggers and bindings in C# isolated and Python v2 with identity-based connections. Configure host.json and app settings, deploy with azd, zip and Flex package deployment and GitHub Actions, and expose tools through the Functions MCP extension.

articles.title: Workflow orchestration on Azure: Durable Functions, Durable Task Scheduler and Logic Apps
articles.scope: Code-first orchestrations (chaining, fan-out/fan-in, async HTTP, monitor, human interaction, entities) with replay determinism vs Logic Apps designer workflows with connectors and agentic workflows. Compares state backends (Azure Storage vs Durable Task Scheduler Dedicated and Consumption SKUs, task hubs, dashboard, emulator, Durable Task SDKs on any compute), observability and cost.

articles.title: Azure Logic Apps in depth: Consumption vs Standard, connectors, securing workflows, hybrid deployment and agentic workflows
articles.scope: Multitenant Consumption vs single-tenant Standard (workflow service plan, ASE v3, hybrid deployment on Arc-enabled Kubernetes), stateful vs stateless workflows, built-in vs managed connectors and integration accounts. Secures triggers with SAS callback URLs vs OAuth/Easy Auth, IP and private endpoint restrictions, managed identity connections and secure inputs/outputs, and explains autonomous and conversational agent loops (Consumption agentic workflows in preview).

articles.title: Azure API Management: tiers, policies, gateways and the AI gateway
articles.scope: Classic vs v2 tiers, APIs, products and subscriptions, the inbound/backend/outbound/on-error policy pipeline (rate limits, validate-jwt, caching, transformation), self-hosted gateway, workspaces and developer portal. AI gateway features (token limits and metrics, semantic caching, backend pools with circuit breaking, content safety) for Foundry and other model backends, MCP server exposure and API Center inventory; contrasts with Amazon API Gateway.

articles.title: Caching on Azure compared: Managed Redis vs Cosmos DB integrated cache vs API Management caching vs Front Door vs in-process
articles.scope: Where each cache sits (edge, gateway, data tier, process), consistency and invalidation, item and query caching in the Cosmos DB integrated cache, API Management internal, external and semantic caching for LLM calls, Front Door caching rules and ASP.NET Core HybridCache or Python in-process caches. Decision matrix for AZ-305 'recommend a caching solution'; cache-aside links architecture/patterns.

articles.title: Service Bus vs Event Grid vs Event Hubs vs Queue Storage
articles.scope: Messages vs discrete events vs event streams, push vs pull, ordering, retention and replay, throughput, dead-lettering and cost, with a decision tree for AZ-305 messaging and event-driven questions. AWS counterparts are rated per term and the full pairs live in cloud/compare; links messaging/delivery-semantics and messaging/event-driven-vs-request-response.

articles.title: Azure Service Bus in depth: queues, topics, sessions and dead-lettering
articles.scope: Queues vs topics with SQL and correlation filters, peek-lock vs receive-and-delete, settlement, sessions for FIFO, duplicate detection, scheduled and deferred messages, transactions, dead-letter handling, Standard vs Premium messaging units and geo-replication. ServiceBusProcessor code in C# and Python with Entra authentication and retry policies.

articles.title: Azure Event Grid: system and custom topics, domains, namespaces, filtering and retries
articles.scope: System topics, custom topics and domains vs namespaces (namespace topics, pull and push delivery, MQTT broker), Event Grid vs CloudEvents schemas, subject and advanced filters, retry policy, dead-lettering, managed identity delivery and webhook validation. Publishes custom events from C# and Python and handles them in Functions.

articles.title: Azure Event Hubs: partitions, consumer groups, checkpointing and the Kafka endpoint
articles.scope: Partitions and keys, consumer groups, EventProcessorClient checkpointing, throughput, processing and capacity units, Capture, Schema Registry, the Kafka endpoint and geo-replication. Explains when Event Hubs beats Service Bus or Event Grid; links messaging/redis-streams-vs-kafka.

articles.title: Azure Managed Redis: tiers, clustering, caching patterns, invalidation and vector search
articles.scope: Memory Optimized, Balanced, Compute Optimized and Flash Optimized tiers, OSS cluster policy by default (non-clustered up to 25 GB), zone redundancy by default, Entra auth, active geo-replication and modules. Implements cache-aside, expiration, invalidation and RediSearch vector indexes in C# and Python, and plans migration from Azure Cache for Redis (Enterprise tiers retire March 31, 2027; Basic/Standard/Premium September 30, 2028).

articles.title: Azure SignalR Service vs Azure Web PubSub for real-time apps
articles.scope: Default, Serverless and Classic SignalR modes vs native WebSocket and Socket.IO hosting in Web PubSub, units and scaling, Functions bindings, authentication and private networking. Builds an Angular client against both; links messaging/signalr-websockets and frontend/real-time-ui-streaming for protocols.

articles.title: Azure storage accounts: types, redundancy, failover and encryption
articles.scope: Account types and services (plus Microsoft.FileShares NFS shares outside accounts), LRS vs ZRS vs GRS/RA-GRS vs GZRS/RA-GZRS by copies, failure domain, durability and RPO, redundancy conversion vs migration, and restrictions such as archive only on LRS, GRS and RA-GRS. Covers customer-managed planned and unplanned failover, Microsoft- vs customer-managed keys, encryption scopes and infrastructure encryption.

articles.title: Storage authorization: access keys vs SAS vs stored access policies vs Microsoft Entra RBAC
articles.scope: Shared key, account and service SAS, user delegation SAS, stored access policies, Entra data-plane roles and ABAC, and identity-based access for Azure Files (AD DS, Entra Domain Services, Entra Kerberos). Shows revocation and audit consequences, disabling shared key access, SAS expiration policy and key rotation; maps SAS to S3 presigned URLs.

articles.title: Securing storage accounts: firewall and virtual network rules, private endpoints, trusted services and Defender for Storage
articles.scope: Configure public network access, virtual network rules over service endpoints, IP rules, resource instance rules and the trusted services exception, then private endpoints per sub-resource with private DNS and network security perimeter where supported. Enable Defender for Storage malware scanning and sensitive data threat detection; networking mechanics link cloud/azure/networking.

articles.title: Blob Storage: access tiers, smart tier, lifecycle rules, versioning, soft delete and immutability
articles.scope: Hot, cool (30-day), cold (90-day) and archive (180-day, offline) tiers with early-deletion charges, default account tier (hot, cool or cold), rehydration with standard or high priority (up to 15 hours), smart tier, lifecycle rules and Storage Actions. Configures soft delete, versioning, snapshots, point-in-time restore, change feed, object replication and immutable storage, compared with S3 classes, Lifecycle and Object Lock.

articles.title: Azure Files and Azure File Sync: SMB, NFS, management models, identity-based access and snapshots
articles.scope: Classic shares vs Microsoft.FileShares NFS shares, SMB vs NFS (NFS SSD-only with LRS/ZRS), SSD and HDD with provisioned v2, v1 and pay-as-you-go billing, identity-based access, share snapshots (up to 200), soft delete, Azure Backup and File Sync cloud tiering. When to choose Azure NetApp Files or Blob NFS, with FSx and EFS mappings.

articles.title: Azure Data Lake Storage: hierarchical namespace, ACLs and analytics access
articles.scope: Data Lake Storage as Blob Storage capabilities unlocked by the hierarchical namespace rather than a separate account type: directories, atomic rename, POSIX-like ACLs with RBAC, ABFS and the dfs endpoint, and feature-support differences. Integration with Fabric shortcuts, Databricks and Synapse, contrasted with S3 plus Lake Formation.

articles.title: Choosing an Azure data store: relational, document, key-value, cache, blob and analytics
articles.scope: Workload-driven selection across Azure SQL, PostgreSQL and MySQL flexible server, Cosmos DB APIs, Azure DocumentDB, Table Storage, Managed Redis, Blob/ADLS and Fabric, balancing features, performance, consistency, durability and cost as AZ-305 asks. Includes Queue and Table Storage positioning and AWS counterparts with fidelity.

articles.title: Azure SQL deployment options: SQL Database vs Managed Instance vs SQL Server on Azure VMs vs SQL database in Fabric
articles.scope: Management scope (database, instance, OS), engine compatibility (SQL Agent, cross-database queries, CLR), networking, licensing and Hybrid Benefit, and the lift-and-shift vs modernize migration target. Positions SQL database in Fabric and maps options to RDS for SQL Server, RDS Custom and Aurora.

articles.title: Azure SQL purchasing models, service tiers and scaling: DTU vs vCore, General Purpose vs Business Critical vs Hyperscale
articles.scope: DTU vs vCore, the General Purpose, Business Critical and Hyperscale architectures, provisioned vs serverless compute, elastic pools and elastic jobs. Covers AZ-305 database scalability: scaling, read scale-out, Hyperscale named and HA replicas and sharding.

articles.title: Securing Azure SQL: Entra-only authentication, TDE with CMK, Always Encrypted, masking, row-level security, auditing, ledger and Defender for SQL
articles.scope: Configure Entra-only authentication, firewall rules vs private endpoints, TDE with service- or customer-managed keys, Always Encrypted with secure enclaves, dynamic data masking and row-level security. Enable auditing for SQL Database and Managed Instance, ledger tables and Defender for SQL vulnerability assessment and threat protection.

articles.title: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server: tiers, high availability, replicas, pooling and elastic clusters
articles.scope: Burstable, General Purpose and Memory Optimized compute, Premium SSD and SSD v2 storage, zone-redundant vs same-zone HA, read and geo replicas, backups, built-in PgBouncer, Entra auth and the migration service. Positions elastic clusters as the target for Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL (on a retirement path, not for new projects) and HorizonDB (preview); maps to RDS and Aurora PostgreSQL.

articles.title: PostgreSQL for AI apps: schema design, pgvector and pg_diskann indexing, filtered RAG and connection optimization
articles.scope: Model documents, chunks and embeddings (vector vs halfvec), choose HNSW vs IVFFlat vs pg_diskann and tune them to cut latency and compute, and size compute, memory and storage for vector workloads. Implement metadata-filtered similarity search and RAG retrieval, in-database embeddings with azure_ai, and pooling in Npgsql and psycopg.

articles.title: Azure Database for MySQL flexible server: tiers, high availability, replicas and when to choose it
articles.scope: Burstable, General Purpose and Business Critical compute, storage autogrow and IOPS, zone-redundant and same-zone HA, read replicas, backups, Entra auth and data-in replication. Short AZ-305 positioning page against PostgreSQL and Azure SQL, mapped to RDS and Aurora MySQL.

articles.title: Azure Cosmos DB core concepts: APIs, request units, partitioning and consistency
articles.scope: API choice (NoSQL, MongoDB RU, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table) vs Azure DocumentDB, RU economics, provisioned vs autoscale vs serverless, logical vs physical partitions and hierarchical keys, five consistency levels, multi-region writes and conflicts, indexing, TTL, integrated cache and periodic vs continuous backup, contrasted with DynamoDB.

articles.title: Cosmos DB for NoSQL in AI apps: SDK queries, RU tuning, vector and hybrid search, change feed
articles.scope: Connect with the C# and Python SDKs using Entra data-plane RBAC, write parameterized queries, reduce RU charge with indexing, consistency and priority-based execution, and store embeddings with vector policies and flat, quantizedFlat or DiskANN indexes. Run VectorDistance, full-text and hybrid RRF queries and a change feed processor.

articles.title: Vector search on Azure data services: Cosmos DB vs DocumentDB vs PostgreSQL vs Managed Redis
articles.scope: Index algorithms, filtering, hybrid search, scale, consistency with operational data and cost per store, ending with a short 'when to graduate to a dedicated search service' section that links ai/platforms for Azure AI Search. Links ai/applied for RAG concepts.

articles.title: Microsoft Fabric, OneLake and Azure Synapse Analytics: an orientation
articles.scope: Orients Fabric (OneLake, shortcuts, lakehouse, warehouse, Real-Time Intelligence, Data Factory, mirroring, capacities) and Synapse (SQL pools, Spark pools, pipelines) and why new investment goes to Fabric. Synapse Link for Cosmos DB is no longer supported for new projects; Cosmos DB mirroring in Fabric replaces it.

articles.title: Azure data integration and analytics compared: Data Factory, Fabric, Databricks, Synapse, Stream Analytics, Data Explorer and mirroring
articles.scope: Batch vs streaming vs zero-ETL mirroring, orchestration vs transformation engines, Spark vs SQL vs KQL analytics, pricing models and Purview governance, giving AZ-305 paths for 'data integration' and 'data analysis'. AWS counterparts (Glue, EMR, Managed Service for Apache Flink, Redshift, zero-ETL) are rated in cloud/compare.

articles.title: Disaster recovery for Azure data services
articles.scope: Recovery-objective-driven DR for Blob (operational vs vaulted backup, object replication, failover), Azure Files, Azure SQL (PITR, LTR, geo-restore, active geo-replication, failover groups), Cosmos DB, PostgreSQL/MySQL and Managed Redis. Links the Backup how-to here, Site Recovery in cloud/azure/compute and architecture/reliability.

articles.title: High availability for Azure data services: zone redundancy, replicas and composite SLAs
articles.scope: In-region HA for relational data (zone-redundant SQL tiers, Business Critical and Hyperscale replicas, Managed Instance, PostgreSQL and MySQL HA), semi-structured data (Cosmos DB zones and multi-region) and unstructured data (ZRS, GZRS, Files). Teaches SLA composition and the HA vs DR boundary for AZ-305.

articles.title: Azure Backup for data services: Backup vault vs Recovery Services vault, operational vs vaulted backup, immutability and MUA
articles.scope: Create vaults and policies for Blob (operational and vaulted), Azure Files (snapshot and vaulted), disks, PostgreSQL flexible server with Cross Region Restore and AKS, then restore and test. Harden with soft delete, immutable vaults, multi-user authorization via Resource Guard, CMK and RBAC, plus backup reports and alerts; VM backup and Site Recovery belong to cloud/azure/compute.

articles.title: Moving and migrating data to Azure: AzCopy, Storage Explorer, File Sync, Storage Mover, Data Box and Database Migration Service
articles.scope: Online vs offline transfer by size, bandwidth and frequency: AzCopy and Storage Explorer, File Sync, Storage Mover for SMB/NFS shares, Data Box Next-gen (120 TB and 525 TB; Data Box Heavy retired) and Database Migration Service. Maps to DataSync, Snowball, Transfer Family and DMS; strategy links architecture/migration.

articles.title: Securing data services end to end on Azure: Storage, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, PostgreSQL and Synapse/Fabric
articles.scope: Layered SC-100 design: identity (Entra-only, disabled key/local auth, Cosmos DB data-plane RBAC), isolation (private endpoints, managed VNets, network security perimeter), encryption (CMK in Key Vault or Managed HSM, Always Encrypted, double encryption), monitoring (Defender for Storage and Databases, logs to Sentinel) and Purview classification. Cross-provider architecture stays in security/data-protection.

articles.title: Azure Monitor data platform: metrics, logs, traces, activity log and diagnostic settings
articles.scope: Platform metrics vs resource logs vs activity log, diagnostic settings, data collection rules and the Azure Monitor Agent, Logs ingestion API, Azure Monitor workspace for Prometheus and OpenTelemetry metrics, and OTLP ingestion. Recommends AZ-305 routing designs and maps each piece to CloudWatch and CloudTrail.

articles.title: Log Analytics workspace design: topology, table plans, retention, access and cost
articles.scope: Single vs multiple workspaces, regional and tenant factors, Analytics vs Basic vs Auxiliary plans, interactive vs long-term retention, summary rules, commitment tiers and dedicated clusters, resource-context vs workspace RBAC, and coexistence with Sentinel and its data lake.

articles.title: KQL for Azure engineers: from first query to joins, time series and alerts
articles.scope: Tabular operators (where, project, extend, summarize, join, union, mv-expand, parse), bin and make-series, render, let and functions, with recipes for App Service, AKS, Container Apps, Functions, Storage and Service Bus logs and alert queries. Ends with a cheatsheet and a KQL vs CloudWatch Logs Insights vs SQL contrast.

articles.title: Application Insights with OpenTelemetry: distributed tracing in .NET and Python
articles.scope: Workspace-based Application Insights with connection strings, the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro for ASP.NET Core and Python, custom spans, metrics and logs, sampling, application map, transaction search, live metrics and standard availability tests (URL ping tests retire September 30, 2028). Traces a request across Container Apps, Service Bus and Functions and adds token, latency and safety telemetry for model calls.

articles.title: Azure Monitor alerts: rule types, action groups and alert processing rules
articles.scope: Metric (static and dynamic thresholds), log search, activity log, Prometheus, service health and resource health alerts, stateful vs stateless behavior, action groups, alert processing rules for suppression and routing, and Azure Monitor Baseline Alerts. Maps to CloudWatch alarms and SNS.

articles.title: Visualizing Azure Monitor data: workbooks vs Azure dashboards vs dashboards with Grafana vs Azure Managed Grafana
articles.scope: Compares workbooks, portal dashboards, built-in Azure Monitor dashboards with Grafana and Azure Managed Grafana by data sources, sharing and RBAC, alerting, IaC and cost. Maps to CloudWatch dashboards and Amazon Managed Grafana; collection lives in the insights how-to.

articles.title: Azure Service Health and Resource Health: service issues, planned maintenance, advisories and health alerts
articles.scope: Distinguishes the Azure status page, Service Health (service issues, planned maintenance, health and security advisories for your subscriptions) and Resource Health (per-resource availability), and wires health alerts to action groups. Maps to the AWS Health Dashboard (close).

articles.title: Azure Monitor insights for VMs, containers, storage and networks
articles.scope: Enable VM monitoring with the Azure Monitor Agent and DCRs, choosing enhanced monitoring with OpenTelemetry guest metrics in an Azure Monitor workspace (recommended) vs classic logs-based VM insights, then Container insights with managed Prometheus, Storage insights and Network insights. Interprets CPU, memory, disk and network indicators and deploys baseline alerts via Policy.

articles.title: Monitoring the delivery pipeline with Azure Monitor: release annotations, alert-based checks and pipeline event alerts
articles.scope: Write Application Insights release annotations from Azure Pipelines and GitHub Actions, gate environments with the Query Azure Monitor alerts check, create work items or issues from alerts, and alert on pipeline and workflow events through service hooks, webhooks and Logic Apps. DORA theory links devops/sre.

articles.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud: CNAPP, Foundational vs Defender CSPM, secure score and compliance
articles.scope: CSPM, DevSecOps and CWPP pillars, Foundational vs Defender CSPM (attack paths, cloud security explorer, agentless scanning, DSPM, AI-SPM), secure score, MCSB and regulatory compliance, AWS/GCP connectors and Arc, the Data and AI security dashboard and the Defender portal experience alongside Exposure Management. Maps to Security Hub CSPM, GuardDuty and Inspector.

articles.title: Defender for Cloud workload protection plans reference
articles.scope: Per-plan reference for Servers P1/P2, Containers, Storage, Databases, App Service, Key Vault, Resource Manager, APIs and AI services: detections, prerequisites, agents vs agentless, pricing unit and AWS counterpart with fidelity.

articles.title: Onboard and configure Defender for Servers across Azure, Arc, AWS and GCP

articles.title: Protecting AI apps and agents with Microsoft security services: Defender for AI services, AI-SPM, Copilot Studio agent protection and the Data and AI security dashboard
articles.scope: Enable Defender for AI services threat protection (prompt injection, jailbreak, data exposure) on Foundry and Azure OpenAI resources, inventory AI assets and attack paths with AI-SPM, enable runtime protection for Copilot Studio agents and monitor the Data and AI security dashboard. articles.title: Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management and Microsoft Security Exposure Management
articles.scope: How Defender EASM discovers and scores internet-facing assets from seeds, versus Exposure Management's exposure graph, attack surface map, critical assets, attack paths, initiatives, metrics and insights. Positions both against Defender CSPM attack paths and Secure Score.

articles.title: Microsoft Defender XDR and unified security operations in the Defender portal

articles.title: Ingesting data into Microsoft Sentinel: connectors, AMA and DCRs, WEF, Syslog/CEF, Azure activity, threat intelligence and retention tiers

articles.title: Detection engineering and automation in Sentinel and Defender XDR
articles.scope: Build scheduled, NRT, threat intelligence and ML analytics rules and XDR custom detections, configure anomalies, tune grouping and suppression and measure MITRE ATT&CK coverage. Automate with automation rules and Logic Apps playbooks and act on SOC optimization recommendations.

articles.scope: Investigate unified incidents from Office 365, Identity, Cloud Apps, Entra ID, Purview, Defender for Cloud and Sentinel with attack stories, embedded Security Copilot and case management. articles.title: Microsoft Security Copilot: capacity, workspaces, roles, plugins and agents

articles.title: Securing Azure application platform services: App Service, Functions, Logic Apps, Container Apps, ACI, ACR and API Management back ends

articles.title: Microsoft Purview orientation for Azure architects

VNet integration only routes the app's outbound calls into a VNet; a private endpoint gives the app a private inbound IP.

SQL Database is database-scoped with serverless, Hyperscale and elastic pools; Managed Instance is instance-scoped with SQL Agent, cross-database queries and VNet placement.
Business Critical keeps data on local SSD with a quorum of replicas for low latency; Hyperscale separates compute from page servers for 128 TB and fast scaling.
DTU bundles compute, memory and I/O into fixed levels; vCore sizes them independently and unlocks Hybrid Benefit, reservations, serverless and Hyperscale.
Active geo-replication fails over single databases manually with connection changes; failover groups fail over sets of databases or a Managed Instance behind stable listeners.
TDE encrypts files at rest but the engine sees plaintext; Always Encrypted keeps column keys on the client so DBAs and the engine never see plaintext.
Session guarantees read-your-writes per client at normal RU cost; strong gives linearizable reads at higher latency and double read RUs, and excludes multi-region writes.
The RU API runs on the Cosmos DB engine with RU billing and global distribution; DocumentDB is a vCore cluster on the open-source DocumentDB engine.
Mirroring replicates operational data into OneLake and is GA; Synapse Link is no longer supported for new projects.
Backup vaults protect newer workloads such as Blob, disks, PostgreSQL and AKS; Recovery Services vaults protect VMs, SQL in VMs, Azure Files and MARS and support Site Recovery.
Operational backup keeps restore data in the source account, so it is lost if the account is deleted; vaulted backup copies data to an isolated vault.
The activity log records control-plane operations automatically for 90 days; resource logs capture data-plane activity and are lost unless a diagnostic setting routes them.
A diagnostic setting routes platform logs and metrics from a resource; a DCR defines agent or API collection with ingestion-time KQL transformations.
Log Analytics stores logs queried with KQL; an Azure Monitor workspace stores Prometheus and OpenTelemetry metrics queried with PromQL.
Application Insights is the APM layer for instrumentation, application map and failure analysis; the workspace is where its telemetry is stored.
An action group says who to notify and what to run; an alert processing rule changes which action groups fire, or suppresses them, across many alerts.
Service Health reports platform incidents and maintenance for services and regions you use; Resource Health reports whether one specific resource is available.
Managed Grafana is a paid dedicated instance with plugins and external sources; dashboards with Grafana are free, portal-native and limited to Azure data.
Defender for Cloud finds misconfigurations and workload threats; Sentinel ingests those alerts with other logs to correlate incidents, hunt and automate response.
Defender for Cloud protects cloud resources and posture; Defender XDR protects endpoints, email, identities and SaaS apps, and both feed one Defender portal incident queue.
Foundational CSPM gives free recommendations and secure score; Defender CSPM adds attack paths, security explorer, agentless scanning, DSPM and AI-SPM.
Secure score measures cloud resource posture in Defender for Cloud; Microsoft Secure Score measures Microsoft 365, identity and device posture.
EASM looks outside-in at internet-facing assets; Exposure Management unifies internal and external exposure data into attack paths, initiatives and metrics.
Automation rules do simple incident triage in Sentinel; playbooks are Logic Apps workflows for multi-step response, often launched by automation rules.
Analytics rules query workspace data; custom detections run advanced hunting over XDR and Sentinel tables and can take device or user actions.
The analytics tier supports real-time detections and interactive KQL at higher cost; the data lake keeps long-retention data cheaply for KQL jobs and notebooks.
Soft delete is always on and recoverable, though an admin can purge; purge protection irreversibly blocks purging until retention expires.
RBAC scopes per object, works with PIM and is the default from API 2026-02-01; access policies are vault-wide, and a Contributor can grant themselves data access.
Premium vaults are multitenant with HSM-backed keys plus secrets and certificates; Managed HSM is single-tenant, keys only, with local RBAC and a customer security domain.
Managed HSM is fully managed and integrates with Azure services for CMK; Cloud HSM is customer-administered for PKCS#11, JCE or CNG apps.
Key Vault protects secrets, keys and certificates with HSM options and rotation; App Configuration stores non-secret settings and flags and references Key Vault for secrets.
A sensitivity label controls access, encryption and marking; a retention label controls how long content is kept and whether it is deleted or declared a record.
Both use the same Resource Manager engine with no state file; Bicep is a concise, type-checked DSL with modules that compiles to ARM JSON.
Incremental leaves resources missing from the template in place; complete deletes them from the resource group, which deployment stacks now handle more safely.
A deployment stack manages deployed resources, with delete or detach on update and deny settings; a template spec only stores and versions the template.
DefaultAzureCredential probes a chain of sources and suits development; ManagedIdentityCredential targets one identity predictably and suits production.
Hosted agents are fresh shared VMs with no private network reach; Managed DevOps Pools run Microsoft-managed agents in your subscription and VNet with custom images.
Both gate merges, but branch policies add linked work items and build validation pipelines, while GitHub uses status checks, rulesets and CODEOWNERS.
Machine Configuration is Policy-driven for Azure and Arc machines; State Configuration is a DSC pull server retiring September 30, 2027.
A reservation commits to a resource family and region for the deepest discount; a savings plan commits hourly spend across eligible compute for a smaller discount.

Both are 1- or 3-year hourly commitments; compute covers VMs, App Service, Functions Premium, ACI and Container Apps, while databases covers Azure SQL, open-source databases, Cosmos DB and SQL licenses.
The pricing calculator estimates the cost of Azure services you plan to run; the TCO calculator compares on-premises ownership costs with Azure.
